differences.new: GitHub LinkedIn Email Patchlamp · the toy The toy and the real thing The real thing The owner of a small business texts a number. Patch, the operator, opens the site's files, makes the change, checks that it is live and texts back, usually in a minute. Patch is Claude wearing a name tag that says Patch. What the toy shows Text Patch from the phone and the thing on the line changes: the storefront, the platen, the belt or the lamp. Patch works on the jack the cord is in, and says so when you ask for something on another. The real Patch works inside a walled-off folder that holds only that client's things. “Undo that” puts the last change back, as it does for real. Ask the toy for something it does not know and Patch points you to Taylor's mailbox. The real Patch passes out-of-scope asks to Taylor. What the toy leaves out The phone is scripted. No model is called, and nothing you type leaves your browser. The real Patch runs Claude Code. The toy answers in a few seconds. The real one usually answers in a minute. Real texts come by SMS, Telegram or Discord. The facts Live since September 2026. More than 1,800 commits and 300 test files across the three codebases as of November 2026. Built and run by one person, me, working with Claude: I own the architecture, the review and the verification. See Patchlamp Every price, published on purpose How it is built, on GitHub Résumé The workshop How this was built I built this workshop working with Claude. It is a static site. Three.js draws the bench, Rapier moves the loose parts, the phone is scripted, and nothing you do here leaves your browser. Tests 2,665 passed on November 22, 2026
